skill.name: multi-agent-patterns
skill.description: Design multi-agent architectures for complex tasks using supervisor, swarm, or hierarchical patterns, with guidance for handoffs, consensus, context isolation, and failure recovery.
skill.summary: Design coordinated multi-agent systems that isolate context, divide work, and recover from failures.
skill.author: Asmayaseen

security_audit.summary: The command, reconnaissance, sensitive-file, and network alerts are false positives caused by Markdown syntax, ordinary Python expressions, prose, and documentation links. Three filesystem examples construct write paths from unsanitized identifiers and can escape the intended workspace when copied into applications. No prompt injection or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: Shared-state and checkpoint examples interpolate identifiers directly into file paths.
remediation.suggestion: Validate identifiers, resolve paths with pathlib, and reject any resolved path outside the configured workspace or checkpoint directory.

remediation.issue: The lock example uses a caller-provided resource name and a non-atomic existence check before writing.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict resource names, create the lock directory safely, and acquire locks atomically with exclusive file creation.

content.value_statement: Complex AI workflows can exceed one agent's context and coordination capacity. This skill guides architecture selection, context isolation, handoffs, consensus, and failure recovery.
actual_capabilities: Compares supervisor, peer-to-peer, and hierarchical architectures by control, scalability, and coordination needs.
Guides task decomposition and context isolation across specialized agents.
Provides implementation patterns for LangGraph, AutoGen, and CrewAI-style systems.
Designs handoffs, weighted voting, debate protocols, checkpoints, retries, and circuit breakers.
Includes Python utilities for messaging, supervision, handoffs, consensus, and failure handling.
limitations: Framework examples require adaptation, dependencies, authentication, and production integration.
The skill does not deploy agents, call models, or benchmark a completed system.
Token multipliers and model comparisons are illustrative and may become outdated.
Filesystem examples require path validation and atomic locking before production use.

use_cases.title: Plan a research workflow
use_cases.description: Divide research, analysis, verification, and writing across agents with clear result aggregation.

use_cases.title: Design a support router
use_cases.description: Route billing, technical, sales, and general requests through explicit agent handoffs.

use_cases.title: Review production resilience
use_cases.description: Assess bottlenecks, divergence, error propagation, retry behavior, checkpoints, and human oversight.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend a supervisor, swarm, or hierarchical architecture for [task]. Explain the choice, agent roles, and handoff points.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner selection for a new multi-agent workflow

prompt_templates.title: Define agent responsibilities
prompt_templates.prompt: Design agents for [workflow] with isolated context. Specify each objective, inputs, tools, outputs, and completion criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Plan coordination and recovery
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a coordination plan for [system]. Include state ownership, message schemas, consensus rules, timeouts, retries, checkpoints, and circuit breakers.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a production design
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [architecture description]. Identify context bottlenecks, unsafe handoffs, convergence risks, error propagation, token costs, and concrete improvements.

output_examples.input: Choose an architecture for a research report that needs web research, analysis, fact-checking, and writing.
output: Recommended pattern: Supervisor architecture with four specialized workers.
The supervisor assigns independent research tasks and aggregates validated summaries.
A fact-checker reviews claims before the writer receives approved evidence.

output_examples.input: Design handoffs for a customer support system covering billing, technical support, sales, and general questions.
output: A triage agent classifies the request and selects one specialist.
Each handoff includes the request, customer context, reason, priority, and required response.
Unknown requests return to the general agent, while repeated failures trigger human review.

output_examples.input: Review a swarm that often loops between two agents and produces inconsistent answers.
output: Add a shared objective, explicit transfer conditions, and a maximum handoff count.
Store decisions in shared state and reject handoffs without new evidence.
Use independent critique before consensus and escalate unresolved conflicts to a coordinator.

best_practices: Use multiple agents only when context isolation or parallel work justifies the added cost.
Define typed handoffs, output validation, ownership, timeouts, and termination conditions before implementation.
Test agent failures, conflicting outputs, stale state, retry exhaustion, and supervisor saturation.
anti_patterns: Do not create agents only to imitate organizational job titles.
Do not pass complete histories to every agent when a bounded task specification is sufficient.
Do not accept majority consensus without confidence, evidence, or independent critique.

faq.question: When should I use more than one agent?
faq.answer: Use multiple agents when tasks decompose cleanly, require different tools, or exceed one context window. Simple workflows usually need one agent.

faq.question: Which architecture should I choose first?
faq.answer: Choose a supervisor for controlled decomposition, a swarm for flexible handoffs, or a hierarchy for layered planning and execution.

faq.question: Does this skill install an agent framework?
faq.answer: No. It provides design guidance, examples, and local Python coordination utilities. You must install and configure any chosen framework.

faq.question: How does the skill reduce context pressure?
faq.answer: It assigns bounded subtasks to agents with separate context windows. Agents return structured results instead of sharing every intermediate message.

faq.question: How should agents resolve disagreement?
faq.answer: Use weighted voting or structured debate with evidence and independent critique. Define an escalation path when agents cannot converge.

faq.question: Are the filesystem examples production ready?
faq.answer: No. Validate path components, enforce directory containment, use atomic locks, control permissions, and protect checkpoint data before production use.
